title: On Entries config page, focus search field by default
line: The search field in System Tray settings is focused when the window opens, so you can type right away to find an entry.
explanation: The Entries list on the System Tray settings page has a search field in its header, but nothing gave it focus when the window opened, so typing did nothing until you clicked it. The search field now calls forceActiveFocus() when it is created, so typing filters the entries straight away.

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: focus the Entries search field when settings open

The search field above the list of System Tray entries had no focus when
the settings window opened, so you had to click it before typing to find
an entry. It now takes focus when created, so you can just start typing.

BUG: 467689

media.caption: Settings just opened, typed "blue": nothing happens, the search field has no focus
Settings just opened, typed "blue": it goes into the focused search field and the list is filtered

review.text: Calling forceActiveFocus() on completion of the Entries Kirigami.SearchField in ConfigGeneral.qml cleanly fixes the retitled wish so users can start filtering System Tray entries immediately upon opening settings. Because the SearchField lives inside an InlineViewHeader ActionToolBar displayComponent nested in a ScrollViewKCM ListView, forceActiveFocus() is appropriate and verified to work both on initial open and when switching back from Keyboard Shortcuts without breaking Tab navigation or the comboboxes above. As a minor optional polish, guarding with !Kirigami.InputMethod.willShowOnActive would avoid popping up a virtual keyboard on touch/tablet devices, though the patch is acceptable as-is.

Does exactly what the current title (Nate's retitle) asks: the Entries SearchField, the action's displayComponent and so the single full delegate in Kirigami's ToolBarLayout, takes focus on creation, and the after screenshot shows typing filtering the list straight away. With the Entries list now merged into the General page this is still sensible, since the list is the page's main content and the comboboxes above stay reachable with Shift+Tab or the mouse. It's a one-line, low-risk QML change, and the commit message and explanation match the diff. If the field overflows into the More menu, the menu's Loader copy grabs focus when it opens, which is harmless.
